Checks that Core API is reachable

502.description: Core API is unreachable or CORE_API_URL is not set

post.summary: Signs a user in
post.description: Forwards the credentials to Core API. The session is only delivered in HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies: `accessToken` (the access JWT, path /) and `refreshToken` (path /auth, read by /auth/refresh and /auth/logout). No token is returned in the body or in a response header.

200.description: Signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

202.description: No session is open. `2fa_required`: the account is protected by a second factor, send the `token` with a code to `POST /auth/login/2fa` within five minutes. `2fa_setup_required` (MAIR-808): the instance makes the second factor mandatory and the account has none, enrol through `POST /auth/2fa/setup` then `POST /auth/2fa/confirm`.

412.description: First sign-in: the password must be changed

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: Instance misconfigured: CORE_API_URL or the session key (JWT_PUBLIC_KEY) is not set, or one of them is invalid

post.summary: Requests a password reset e-mail
post.description: Forwards the e-mail to Core API (POST /api/v1/auth/forgot_password), which e-mails a one-time reset link (`<PUBLIC_URL>/reset-password?token=…`, valid 15 minutes) when the address matches an active account. The answer is the same empty 200 whether the address matches an account or not, so it never tells which e-mails are registered. Every request counts against two budgets (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_FORGOT_PASSWORD_MAX, 10 per 15 minutes by default): one per e-mail address, and one per client IP when TRUST_PROXY is set and the request carries X-Forwarded-For. Malformed requests also count as failed attempts per client IP. The client IP is relayed to Core API, which limits the requests per client and per e-mail address too.

200.description: Request accepted, empty body. Does not tell whether an e-mail was sent.

400.description: Invalid payload (missing `email`, or not an e-mail address of at most 320 characters)

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable, or it could not send the e-mail

503.description: Instance misconfigured: CORE_API_URL or the session key (JWT_PUBLIC_KEY) is not set, or one of them is invalid

post.summary: Resets a password with the e-mailed token
post.description: Forwards the reset token of the e-mail, the new password and the device to Core API (POST /api/v1/auth/reset_password), which saves the password, revokes every other session of the account and opens a new one. The session is then set exactly like POST /auth/login (HttpOnly `accessToken` and `refreshToken` cookies): the user is signed in. The token is single use: a second reset with it answers 401. Failed attempts are rate limited per client IP when TRUST_PROXY is set and the request carries X-Forwarded-For.

200.description: Password reset and signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

202.description: Password reset, but no session is open (the mailbox is not a second factor): `2fa_required` sends the `token` with a code to `POST /auth/login/2fa`, `2fa_setup_required` (mandatory policy, MAIR-808) to `POST /auth/2fa/setup`.

400.description: Invalid payload (`token` not a UUID, `new_password` not 12 to 255 characters or refused by the Core API password policy, `device_info` longer than 512 characters, or a control character)

401.description: Reset token unknown, expired or already used, or account archived since the e-mail was sent; request a new e-mail.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: Instance misconfigured: CORE_API_URL or the session key (JWT_PUBLIC_KEY) is not set, or one of them is invalid

post.summary: Renews the access JWT
post.description: Exchanges the refresh token of the session (body field, else the HttpOnly `refreshToken` cookie set at sign-in) for a new access JWT (Core POST /api/v1/sessions/refresh), without a session: an expired JWT can be renewed. Core rotates the refresh token: like /auth/login, the new JWT and the new refresh token are only delivered in the HttpOnly accessToken and refreshToken cookies. Failed attempts are rate limited per refresh token, and per client IP when TRUST_PROXY is set and the request carries X-Forwarded-For. The request's User-Agent is sent to Core as the device of the renewal: Core writes it to the sign-in journal and the alert e-mails when a replaced refresh token is reused, which closes the whole session (401). A token another front of the same browser replaced a few seconds ago answers 409: nothing changed, replay the request with the cookies that renewal set.

200.description: JWT renewed; the new access JWT is in the accessToken cookie and the rotated refresh token in the refreshToken cookie (the one sent no longer works).

400.description: Invalid payload, or no refresh token in the body nor in the refreshToken cookie

401.description: Refresh token unknown, revoked or expired, or replaced by a renewal more than 10 seconds ago: Core then closes the whole session (reuse of a stolen token) and e-mails the agent and the administrators

409.description: Refresh token replaced by a concurrent renewal of the same session less than 10 seconds ago (Core `refresh_superseded`): nothing changed and no cookie is set; replay the request with the cookies that renewal set instead of signing the user out.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: Instance misconfigured: CORE_API_URL or the session key (JWT_PUBLIC_KEY) is not set, or one of them is invalid

post.summary: Signs a user out
post.description: Revokes the caller's Core API session: with the refresh token (body field or refreshToken cookie) through POST /api/v1/auth/logout, which needs no JWT and so also works once the access JWT has expired (MAIR-692), and, when the session (`Authorization: Bearer` header) is sent, from the JWT through POST /api/v1/sessions/logout (both together, so a stale refresh token does not leave the JWT's session open). `session_revoked` is true when either succeeded. Without either credential, nothing is revoked. It then always clears the HTTP-only accessToken and refreshToken cookies, even if Core API fails.

500.description: Server error

post.summary: Completes the sign-in of a protected account (second factor)
post.description: Second step of `POST /auth/login` (or `POST /auth/reset_password`) when they answered `202` `2fa_required`: forwards the login token and the code (TOTP or backup code) to Core API. The session is then delivered exactly like `POST /auth/login` (HttpOnly `accessToken` and `refreshToken` cookies). The token is single use and burnt after five wrong codes: restart from the password.

200.description: Signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

401.description: Unknown, expired or burnt login token, or wrong or replayed code. A backup code that was already spent is told apart: two refusals are told apart by `error.details`: `body.code` (message `Backup code already used.`: it still counts as a failed attempt and five burn the token, so the agent can type another backup code only while the login token is still valid; the fifth failed attempt, or an expired token, answers `body.token` instead) and `body.token` (message `Invalid or expired login token.`: the login session is over, restart from the password). A wrong code has no detail.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: The second factor is not configured on this instance (Core has no encryption key), or CORE_API_URL is not set.

post.summary: Passkey sign-in: gets the challenge
post.description: Starts a discoverable passkey sign-in on Core API: the browser offers the passkeys it holds for the site, so nobody types an e-mail. Returns the WebAuthn options and the `id` of the ceremony (single use, two minutes), to send back with the browser answer to `POST /auth/passkey`.

403.description: The administrator does not accept passkeys (two-factor policy).

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: Passkeys are not configured on this instance (Core has no WebAuthn relying party), or CORE_API_URL is not set: the front falls back to the password.

post.summary: Passkey sign-in: sends the browser answer
post.description: Forwards the signed challenge to Core API, which identifies the account by the passkey and verifies it. The session is then delivered exactly like `POST /auth/login` (HttpOnly `accessToken` and `refreshToken` cookies). A passkey is a complete sign-in: no second factor is asked, a mandatory policy is satisfied. Every refusal is the same `401`.

200.description: Signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

401.description: The passkey is refused: unknown, expired or replayed challenge, unknown passkey, bad signature, cloned passkey, archived account.

403.description: The administrator does not accept passkeys (two-factor policy).

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

post.summary: Mandatory enrolment by passkey: gets the challenge
post.description: For an agent who got `202` `2fa_setup_required` (no session yet) and whom the policy lets enrol with a passkey: forwards the enrolment token to Core API, which answers the WebAuthn creation options (discoverable credential and user verification required, any password manager accepted). The token stays valid (five minutes) until the passkey is created. Same refusals as `POST /auth/passkey/setup`.

401.description: Unknown, expired, spent or burnt enrolment token, or archived account.

403.description: The administrator does not accept passkeys (two-factor policy).

409.description: The account already has an active second factor: the token is of no use.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

post.summary: Mandatory enrolment by passkey: sends the browser answer
post.description: Forwards the enrolment token, the label and the browser answer to Core API, which stores the passkey, spends the token and opens the session like `POST /auth/login` (HttpOnly `accessToken` and `refreshToken` cookies). A passkey satisfies the mandatory policy by itself: no backup codes are issued. A refused answer counts like a wrong code and the token is burnt at the fifth.

200.description: Passkey created and signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

400.description: Invalid data, or an answer Core refuses (the same token can try again until it is burnt).

401.description: Unknown, expired, spent or burnt enrolment token, or archived account.

403.description: The administrator does not accept passkeys (two-factor policy).

409.description: The account already has an active second factor, or this credential is already registered.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: Passkeys are not configured on this instance (Core has no WebAuthn relying party), or CORE_API_URL is not set.

post.summary: Mandatory enrolment: starts the registration of the authenticator application
post.description: When the instance makes the second factor mandatory, `POST /auth/login` (or `/auth/reset_password`) answers `202` `2fa_setup_required` for an account without a usable factor. Forwards that token to Core API, which answers the secret and the `otpauth://` URI to register in the authenticator application. No session exists yet: finish with `POST /auth/2fa/confirm`. Calling it again replaces the pending secret.

401.description: Unknown, expired or burnt enrolment token: a single detail points at `body.token` and the agent starts over from the password.

409.description: The account got a second factor meanwhile: sign in normally.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.

500.description: Server error

502.description: Core API unavailable or invalid upstream answer

503.description: The second factor is not configured on this instance (Core has no encryption key), or CORE_API_URL is not set.

post.summary: Mandatory enrolment: confirms with a first code and signs in
post.description: Forwards the enrolment token and the first code of the authenticator application to Core API, which activates the second factor and opens the session, delivered exactly like `POST /auth/login` (HttpOnly `accessToken` and `refreshToken` cookies). The ten single-use backup codes are in the body, once: the front must make the agent keep them. The token is single use and burnt after five wrong codes: restart from the password.

200.description: Enrolled and signed in; the access JWT is in the `accessToken` cookie and the refresh token in the `refreshToken` cookie.

401.description: Wrong first code (no detail: the token stays usable), or unknown, expired or burnt enrolment token (a single detail points at `body.token`: the agent starts over from the password).

404.description: `POST /auth/2fa/setup` was not called with this token.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this client (or for this account); retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Body: `{ "error": { "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "message": "Too many attempts, please try again later", "details": [] } }`.
